newsitem.title: USA: US jet fuel plummets with NYMEX second day in row.
newsitem.headline: US jet fuel plummets with NYMEX second day in row.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel fell three cents a gallon tracking NYMEX futures Thursday, for a two-day loss of over five cents amid a continuing distillate selloff on last week's decent distillate stock build.
Differentials on aviation-quality 54-grade fuel remained stable in especially thin trade, players said.

New York Harbor 54-grade was offered at 0.50 cent over the print. Gulf material was sold at 1.75 cents under the screen in the morning but later firmed 0.25 cent to Wednesday's level, traders said, after a brief spate of buying.
Absolute prices hovered at about 71.40 cents a gallon in New York Harbor and 69.50 cents a gallon in the Gulf Coast.
"Some people were expecting prices to go even higher so maybe they're thinking the worst is over," one New York jet fuel trader said.

Even so, traders pointed out that U.S. jet fuel prices are now about 25 cents a gallon higher than they were this time last year, driven into orbit this year amid concerns about the lowest domestic heating stocks since the early 1970s. -- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
